title: Lattice: Quant Onboarding Sprintlets (week of 2028-05-03)
content:
Purpose: quick, on-the-ground capture for the mini-sprint we ran to validate 4-bit KV-cache behavior and model quality regressions for the new graft-7b onboarding. This is rough — capture of standups, immediate bench results, and action items for next sprintlet.

Attendees:
- Asha (notes)
- Diego (bench engineer)
- Lina (evals lead)
- Marcus (runtime)
- Priya (SRE on call)

1) Yesterday -> Today (standup style)
- Diego: finished baseline microbench for graft-7b (fp16) with our standard 128-token chat workload. Median tail p50/p95 latencies on c5g-16 measured: p50=78ms, p95=220ms (batched, 4-concurrent).
- Marcus: integrated the 4-bit KV-path prototype into the runtime branch and ran a smoke that validated KV restore across session-resume; saw ~12% smaller RAM hotset but a 5-7ms overhead per generation step (investigating vectorized ops).
- Lina: eval harness ran 2k prompt evals across instruction-following benchmarks — raw perplexity delta: +0.9 on XM-Eval subset, but instruction-fluency score (human proxy) unchanged for ~85% of prompts.
- Priya: noticed higher GC churn when microbatching at 16x; spawned pod OOMs on 2/8 nodes in the canary group during the midnight load test.

2) Quick experiment summaries (data + numbers)
- Experiment Q-LAT-0428: graft-7b fp16 vs graft-7b 4-bit-kv (symmetric q4)
  - Dataset: 2k mixed chat prompts (median length 40 tokens, 99th=480 tokens)
  - Throughput: fp16 baseline 1.0x, q4-kv 1.12x (measured tokens/sec increase)
  - Latency: p50 delta -3ms (slightly faster due to smaller mem copies), p95 delta +6ms (extra decode overhead in codegen path)
  - Memory hotset: -11% (KV region)
  - Perplexity delta (LM eval): +0.8 absolute (small, concentrated on long-context prompts)
  - Observations: quality regressions correlate with long prefix reuse; hypothesize quant-noise accumulates in KV repeats.

- Experiment Q-QUAL-0502: eval split by prompt-type (instruction vs. factual)
  - Instruction prompts: BLEU-like instruction adherence metric unchanged for 86% of samples; failure modes are hallucinated step counts or skipped sub-steps.
  - Factual QA: small regression in exact-match (EM) for entity-heavy Qs (5% absolute drop), often when facts appear early in long context.

3) Incidents and oddities
- Node OOMs on pk-124 during microbatch ramp (seen 02:13 UTC). Root cause trace points to transient spike in pinned allocations when KV cache is rebuilt for resumed sessions. Repro steps captured in ENG-8421.
- A reproducible mismatch: on a small subset (n=48) the 4-bit-kv decode produced token-level divergence from fp16 on step 12+ only when the prefix contained repeated enumerations (e.g., lists). Diego will dump kv tensors for failing cases.

4) Hypotheses we want to test next sprintlet
- Hypothesis A: stochastic rounding (instead of naive trunc) for KV compression reduces long-context drift. Test: patch quantizer to use stochastic rounding and run same 2k evals.
- Hypothesis B: microbatching at certain sizes triggers allocator fragmentation — switching to pooled allocator for KV region may reduce OOMs. Priya to prototype.
- Hypothesis C: Slight reordering of kernel invocation (move KV restore before decoder warmup) reduces p95 tail. Marcus to bench.

5) Action items (owners + expected completion)
- Diego: collect KV tensor dumps for 48 failing cases; attach to QON-317 and add short script to replay exact decode path. ETA 2028-05-06.
- Lina: run stochastic-rounding pass over the 2k eval set and produce per-prompt deltas + failure clustering. ETA 2028-05-09.
- Marcus: bench alternative kernel order and report p50/p95 variance across 5 runs; include CPU/GPU timeline traces. ETA 2028-05-07.
- Priya: prototype pooled allocator for KV region on staging; include leak detector and observe overnight soak. ETA 2028-05-10.
- Asha: synthesize canary rollout checklist for graft-7b-quant with rollback triggers and required telemetry (p95 latency + EM drop > 3% => rollback). Draft to linked confluence page. ETA 2028-05-08.

6) Canary/rollout notes (operational thresholds)
- Canary group: 2% traffic, region-us-west1, duration=6h steady-state after warmup.
- Success criteria: no p95 latency regression >10% vs baseline, no EM drop >2% on core QA set, no node-level OOMs or >0.1% error rate.
- Rollback triggers: any single node OOM during canary OR sustained p95 increase >20% for >10m.

7) Open questions / research decisions
- Do we accept a tiny EM/perp regression in exchange for 10-12% unit cost reduction? Lina: need stakeholder signoff from product (GTM impact).
- How to instrument long-context drift in production without PII exposure? Propose synthetic prompt seeds that approximate customer patterns.
- Do we run stochastic rounding per-byte or per-vector? (cost/latency tradeoff).

8) Meeting notes (ad-hoc sync 2028-05-03 16:00 UTC)
- Summary: alignment on running stochastic rounding experiments and prototyping pooled allocator. Agreed to widen the eval harness to include a 'repeat-list' stress subset to catch enumerations failure mode.
- Quick decisions: canary thresholds agreed as above; Asha to draft proper KB entry for SRE on how to triage var-sized OOMs during microbatch ramps.

9) Misc captures / notes to self
- Keep an eye on the kv-prefetch heuristics (recent PR changed default prefetch window to 3). Prefetching + quant noise may interplay.
- Add small unit test: reproducible_token_divergence for graft-7b when decoding with identical RNG seeds.
- Check with product whether 10% unit cost improvement is worth a short-term 1% EM drop for low-risk customer tiers (dedicated non-enterprise).

Appendix: quick commands used for benching
- bench script: ./scripts/bench_local.sh --model graft-7b --mode fp16 --clients 4 --tokens 128
- q4-kv run: ./scripts/bench_local.sh --model graft-7b --quant q4-kv --kv-prefetch 3 --clients 4
- tensor dump helper: python tools/kv_dump.py --session-id $SESSION --out ./dumps/$SESSION

Next sync: brief standup Monday 2028-05-08 09:30 PT; deep dive Thursday 2028-05-10 15:00 PT (stochastic rounding + allocator review).

Status: draft — saving this to capture momentum, will refine after Diego's dumps and Lina's initial eval pass.

-- end of notes --
